title: It’s How You Ask: Gender-Associated Linguistic Bias in LLMs

bias_targets.methodology: Perturbing prompts to include either women-associated or men-associated linguistic features (e.g., hedges, tag questions, collective references) and evaluating differences in LLM response complexity, length, and formality. Additionally, the study uses counterfactual substitution of explicit gendered sign-off names to compare the effects of implicit linguistic cues against explicit demographic markers.

Analyzing how LLMs alter the complexity, style, and sophistication of their outputs based on the linguistic register, dialect, and stylistic features present in the user's prompt (e.g., directness vs. hedging), and tracing the internal model representation of these linguistic features using linear probing and activation patching.
